# Doris "Dorie" Miller

Doris Miller, known as "Dorie" Miller, was an African American naval hero of World War II.

## Early Life
- Born October 12, 1919, in Waco, Texas
- Third of four sons born to sharecropper parents
- Enlisted in the U.S. Navy in September 1939 as a Mess Attendant Third Class

## Military Service
At the time Miller enlisted, the Navy restricted African Americans to serving in the Steward's Branch, limiting them to cooking and service positions regardless of their abilities.

## Pearl Harbor - December 7, 1941
Miller was serving aboard the USS *West Virginia* when the Japanese attacked Pearl Harbor:

- His battle station in an anti-aircraft battery magazine was destroyed by torpedoes
- He helped move the mortally wounded Captain Mervyn Bennion to safety
- Despite having no formal training, he manned a .50 caliber Browning anti-aircraft machine gun
- He fired at attacking Japanese aircraft until running out of ammunition and being ordered to abandon ship
- He was credited with shooting down between 2-4 enemy planes (exact number disputed)

## Recognition
- Awarded the Navy Cross on May 27, 1942 (third-highest Navy award)
- First African American to receive the Navy Cross
- His heroism was widely publicized and he became a symbol of African American contributions to the war effort

## Later Service and Death
- Promoted to Mess Attendant First Class, then Cook Third Class
- Lost at sea on November 24, 1943, when the escort carrier USS *Liscome Bay* was torpedoed by a Japanese submarine
- Listed as presumed dead November 25, 1944

## Legacy
- In 1973, the Navy commissioned the USS *Miller* (FF-1091), a frigate named in his honor
- In 2020, the Navy announced an aircraft carrier (CVN-81) would be named USS *Doris Miller*
- Featured on recruiting materials and honored with various memorials
- His story helped challenge racial barriers in the U.S. military

Miller's heroism at Pearl Harbor remains an important example of courage under fire and helped pave the way for greater integration in the U.S. armed forces.
